panels.title: The granary on the plain
panels.desc: Rows of storehouses on Paxos's plain, tall painted pithoi inside; a second, newer granary catches the light on the higher ground beyond.
panels.scene: High view over the granary storehouses on Paxos's plain, set well apart from one another. Rows of tall painted storage jars are visible through open doors, and clerks move between the buildings with baskets of clay tablets. On the higher ground beyond, a second granary of newer storehouses is just catching the morning light.

panels.title: The granary of Paxos
panels.desc: Rows of tall storage jars in stone storerooms; in separate storehouses, clerks copy identical records onto clay tablets while the steward receives a merchant.
panels.scene: The island's granary: rows of tall painted storage jars (pithoi) in stone storerooms; in three separate storehouse rooms, three clerks sit at identical desks copying identical records onto clay tablets, while at the central storehouse a senior clerk (the steward) receives a merchant with a sack of grain and dictates.
panels.caption: THE GRANARY KEPT ITS RECORDS IN SEVERAL STOREHOUSES AT ONCE — SO THAT ONE FIRE, OR ONE STORM, COULD NOT STOP THE SELLING OF GRAIN.

panels.title: The viewstamp
panels.desc: A clerk presses a two-part cylinder seal into wet clay: one half a steward's sigil, the other a row of tally marks.
panels.scene: Close-up of a clerk's hands pressing a two-part cylinder seal into a wet clay tablet: the left half of the impression shows a steward's personal sigil (a bull's head) and the right half shows a row of tally marks. A tray of already-stamped tablets sits beside it in neat order.
panels.caption: THE VIEWSTAMP: WHICH STEWARD’S TERM, AND HOW MANY RECORDS INTO IT. BY ITSELF A COUNT MEANS NOTHING ONCE THE STEWARD CHANGES.

panels.title: The communication buffer
panels.desc: The steward drops numbered tablets in order down a chute to waiting runners; a knotted bell rope shows how far they've been confirmed received.
panels.scene: The steward clerk drops numbered clay tablets, one after another in order, into a slanted wooden chute that runs out of the window down to runners waiting with baskets; beside the chute a small bell rope marked with a knot shows how far the tablets have been confirmed received.
panels.caption: THE COMMUNICATION BUFFER: RECORDS GO OUT IN ORDER. TO “FORCE” IT IS TO WAIT UNTIL ENOUGH COPYISTS HAVE CAUGHT UP.

panels.title: The view manager's invitation
panels.desc: Stormy night: a clerk hands sealed invitations to runners; at other storehouses, one holds up a full basket of tablets, another a single apologetic sigil.
panels.scene: Stormy night over the granary's storehouses: a clerk in one (the view manager) hands sealed invitation tablets to runners heading out along muddy roads. At the other storehouses, one clerk answers by holding up a full basket of stamped tablets; another, with a bandaged head, holds up a single tablet with only a sigil on it, looking apologetic. A washed-out bridge cuts off one more storehouse in the distance.
panels.cast: the view manager, clerks at each storehouse
panels.caption: THE VIEW MANAGER’S INVITATION. “HERE IS EVERYTHING I KNOW,” SAYS ONE CLERK. “I FELL AND FORGOT EVERYTHING,” SAYS ANOTHER.

panels.title: An ordinary day at the granary
panels.desc: Four beats in one scene: a merchant's request, the steward's stamp, two runners to the copyists, and grain weighed out on the first acknowledgment.
panels.scene: A four-beat sequence arranged left to right in one wide scene: a merchant hands a request tablet to the steward; the steward stamps it and sends copies with two runners to two copyist storehouses; the copyists add it to the end of their shelves and send runners back with small acknowledgment tokens; the steward, holding one token, weighs out grain to the merchant.
panels.cast: the steward, a merchant, two copyist clerks
panels.caption: AN ORDINARY DAY: REQUEST, PREPARE, PREPARE-OK — AND WITH ONE COPYIST’S ACKNOWLEDGMENT, THE STEWARD OF THREE STOREHOUSES MAY WEIGH OUT THE GRAIN.

panels.title: The stale steward
panels.desc: Cut off by a flooded road, the old steward keeps stamping tablets and holding them out; across the water, a copyist turns his back, pointing to a newer sigil.
panels.scene: In a remote storehouse cut off by a flooded road, the old steward keeps stamping PREPARE tablets and holding them out of the window; on the far bank, a copyist folds his arms and turns his back, pointing to a new tablet in his own hand bearing a different, newer steward's sigil.
panels.caption: ONCE A COPYIST HAS SENT HIS LOG TO THE NEW STEWARD, HE ACCEPTS NOTHING MORE FROM THE OLD ONE.

panels.title: The clerk who forgot
panels.desc: A bandaged clerk presses a fresh thumbprint token into clay and sends copies out; a runner returns with a basket of tablets bearing the same print.
panels.scene: A clerk with a bandaged head returns to his empty storehouse desk and presses his thumb into a fresh lump of clay to make a unique token; runners carry copies of the token to the other storehouses, and one returning runner brings back a heavy basket of tablets from the steward, with the same thumbprint token tied to its handle.
panels.caption: THE CLERK WHO FORGOT: ASK A QUORUM, MARK THE QUESTION WITH A FRESH THUMBPRINT, AND TAKE THE RECORDS ONLY FROM THE STEWARD.

panels.title: Moving the granary
panels.desc: A dawn procession moves the records from old, cracked storehouses to new ones on higher ground; an old clerk closes his door only once a new lamp is lit.
panels.scene: A procession at dawn moving the granary records from a row of old, cracked storehouses to a row of new ones on higher ground: clerks carry baskets of tablets along the track between them; lamps are being lit in the new storehouses one by one, and only when a new lamp is lit does an old clerk close and bar his storehouse door.
panels.caption: MOVING THE GRANARY: THE OLD CLERKS KEEP THEIR DOORS OPEN UNTIL ENOUGH NEW STOREHOUSES HAVE LIT THEIR LAMPS.
